tasks.short: Climate pictures from paleoclimate and GIS series stay her choice and her reading.

steps.what: Create the specification for historical or future climate changes
Build visualizations using paleoclimate or climate geographic information systems databases
Judge the picture and illustrate the Earth's climate change

tasks.design: She names the dataset, variable, region, period and chart type on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A script redraws the visualization from those fields and the series in the {DATA_PLATFORM}. She checks the picture against the series and writes what the change means.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each climate picture was drawn by hand in the GIS, including the scale, the comparison and the legend, so a repeat picture waited on that drawing.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she names dataset, variable, region, period and chart type, a script can redraw that picture from the series the GIS already holds. Paper screening, permit text and emissions filings in this group are other tasks, and they are not this picture.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a historical or future change is real in the paleoclimate series, and whether the picture is allowed to show it.
tasks.human_edge: She decides which change the picture may claim. A matching scale does not make a weak series into a real change.
tasks.altitude: Choosing the change stays on her desk. Only the redraw of a picture she has already specified leaves.

reach.task: Compare a remote-sensing scene with the climate series when the change depends on the surface.
reach.learn: Which scene matches the region and period she already named, and which scene does not.

evidence.claim: A script can redraw a chart when the dataset, variable, region, period and chart type are already named.

assumptions: The figure specification has five fields she writes first: dataset, variable, region, period and chart type. The producer is the atmospheric scientist. If a field is missing, she builds the picture herself and the script does not run.
The climate series are already in the {DATA_PLATFORM}. The script reads them there. No second entry of those series is removed.
Incremental upkeep is 4 hours per 100 baseline hours. She keeps dataset ids, variable names and chart defaults when those fields change. That upkeep is not zero.
A one-off picture whose chart type she has not named is outside this saving.
unknowns: Whether her climate pictures repeat a named chart type, or are one-off comparisons.
Whether the GIS exposes dataset, variable, region and period as fields a script can read.
research_questions: Which of her climate pictures repeat a dataset, variable, region, period and chart type she can name before the redraw?

already_counted.description: She still writes the five-field specification and still judges the picture against the series.

incremental.description: She keeps dataset ids, variable names and chart defaults when the GIS fields change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A one-off picture she has not specified before saves nothing, so the low is zero. The high is a repeat picture whose five fields she already named, after 4 hours of upkeep on the defaults, and it stops at 22 because some legends and scales still need her hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Redrawing a specified climate picture leaves part of her week. She gains no right to claim a historical or future change the series does not show.
skills_to_grow: Name dataset, variable, region, period and chart type before a redraw.
Stop when the paleoclimate series does not support the change the picture suggests.
Refuse a visualization that mixes historical and future periods without saying so.
role.ambitious_version: She still chooses which climate change a picture may show, and she still reads every picture against the series. A script only redraws a figure she has already specified. She does not issue a public forecast from the picture.
